rules.basis: V4 (referee, from v4's own sim, sim/scale-probes.test.ts 'short lane (durable)', pinned red): a member writes row x and leaves; another removes x; tombstone GC and compaction drop the remove from the remover's lane while the old write stays the last entry of the leaver's lane; after a restart from its own disk the remover shows x again. So an acknowledged remove does not survive a restart. This is the LWW lane protocol (R lww: per-origin lanes, tombstone collection, merge by stamp); v4 takes no fix (AMENDMENTS 3)

rules.basis: V4: v4's own scoped sweep pins it (STATUS.md, KNOWN_UNSAFE, A2 seed 9). A forwarded write commits at its owner; the owner is cut off before the commit leaves it; the issuer retries and the new owner commits it again; after the heal both commits stand, since LWW merge keeps both (R lww). A write issued from a tap is also committed twice. D win is not the cause: DRAFT, LANE and SPLIT hold D win and are met

Re-ruled (RR-01): E-13 is not a ceiling. The handover meets 10 ms at the median (9.7 and 9.8 ms); the 24 to 31 ms worst cases sit inside this disk's own stalls (22.9 ms in a quiet window with no handover), measured on etcd's Go server, not a port's floor. Earlier reason: AMENDMENTS 1.3, F-05's handover clause: etcd's own leader transfer pauses its group 9.7 to 9.8 ms at the median and 24 to 31 ms at worst on this disk, against 10 ms (TS) and 2 ms (native); a port of the same Raft can only approach that (E-13; gap from 24.4 ms against 10 ms). Restated as 'C plus the longest normal gap between commits plus 5 ms' it is open: the port's handover was not timed, and failover at E = 2 s with 0.25 E jitter sums to 2.5 s with no margin (reasoned, not run; at E = 1 s one native failover took 1.42 s against 1.25 s)

rules.basis: V4: STATUS.md, pinned in sim/leave-harness.ts (stopsOneByOne) and tests/stops.test.ts. Each clean leaver's dir holds the last view it saw, a view it is not in; the last view's only voter is the last to stop; so the first two back sit joining until that one returns, and no kernel rule can re-form them safely. This is v4's own membership by ballot, which comes with R lww (no other axis carries v4's membership)
BUY: JetStream's own Raft groups decide, and should return with any majority; E-44 killed one leader of three, but a full stop and a restart in every order were not run

Any group on Raft, data or metadata (I names a Raft core): from three voters up Raft elects once any majority is back (E-14b: no stuck state with a live majority, 5,165,341 states; E-14c with grow first). A-01 states one limit: while a group grows from two voters to three, for one message, a restart needs the old leader back (model-checked). Read as a two-voter group's limit it is open until v4's stopsOneByOne harness runs on a v5 kernel; read with no room for that window it fails (the alt). ISR and SLOG take the alt through their Raft metadata group, and their own restart orders (the last in-sync set, a loglet's write quorum) were not modelled
OBJ: no group has voters; any process that reaches the store can take the writer lease by compare-and-swap, so restart order should not matter. The lease and the manifest were not modelled

else.basis: not judged: a row with no Raft group whose restart orders were not modelled

parts.why: The alt reading follows any Raft group, data or metadata: the ISR and SLOG judges say 'its metadata group is Raft and takes A-01's two-voter window (so the alt)'. I is the axis that says some group runs Raft. V4's failure is its own membership (R lww).

rules.basis: V4: STATUS.md pins it red in v4's own tests. After tombstone GC and compaction a removed row comes back from a short lane; a write from an evicted member beats a newer remove after a heal; a fresh member's data: seed brings back a deleted seed row. All three are the LWW lane protocol: per-origin lanes, tombstone collection, merge by stamp (R lww)

else.basis: Every other row folds one ordered log per partition, so a remove is an entry every copy folds and v4's lane bugs cannot arise (reasoned). But no experiment ran it: E-33 left erasure out of its restore model, snapshot layers against retention were never modelled, and PD's MVCC tombstones and JetStream's markers were not run either

rules.basis: Every row fero builds can raise a health row and a stderr line, and E-29's pipeline shows two (the 80 % line, a full follower saying so). But no experiment tested a health row, and the evidence names waits that must speak: a member cut from its leader stalled its clients for 20 s on etcd (E-38c; A-02 refuses at once), healing waits while #meta has no leader (E-16), and the two-voter window (A-01). No test per failure kind exists

BUY: losses inside JetStream show as its own advisories, which fero would have to turn into health rows (not built); E-44 found one notice that can be missed: 'deliveries used up' is announced once, on a subject that is not stored

else.basis: not judged: a row with R lww that is not v4 as built. V4's own cell is an override (v4's print paths), so a new LWW row would owe its health lines like any other row

V4.basis: The referee read v4's code: v4 prints a stderr line only for a door or contract refusal, a cut write loop and a fault in user code (api/index.ts); a member that turns read-only as minority or held only flips the writable row of cluster, and a first view that waits on a dead static host says nothing at all (kernel/node.ts). So a loss of writability can last with no line naming the cause and the fix. That is v4's code as built, which no axis tag expresses: a new row with v4's options would write its own health lines

parts.why: Every row is open but V4. The open cells rest on each family's own named waits (fero's kernel waits for the rows fero builds, JetStream's advisories for BUY), so R decides them; V4 fails on what its built code prints, not on an option, so it is an override.

else.basis: AMENDMENTS 1.3, F-10's line: the failed-fsync and directory-fsync clauses are untested for every row, because LazyFS cannot make a sync fail or lose a directory entry, and the line asks for no new wording, so both verdicts are open. The rest is shown for the Raft rows on a journal of L0's shape (E-29: 576 torn tails cut, 0 of 10,020 acknowledged batches lost; E-14b, E-37: a wiped disk never votes under its old id). Z crash rows (PD, ISR, OBJ, V4) rest on what F-22 judges, and are open too

rules.basis: Two machines plus any third voter is a three-voter Raft group: either crash leaves a majority of two, and every acknowledged write is on two of three disks. On etcd's spec three voters with one crash break no invariant and have no stuck state (E-14b); etcd took writes again after a kill -9 of its leader (E-13); the port was linearizable on 3 nodes (E-46); RLOG's writer change holds in E-16. A small full server counts as the third voter, so no witness rule is needed (V not deciding). The two-voter health line is design, not a test

BUY (referee): three nats-server processes with three file replicas and an fsync before each ack lost none of 900 acknowledged writes through a kill of the stream's leader (E-44, measured on the real system). rules.basis: OBJ (referee): OBJ has no voters at all. So no majority can be lost and the command has nothing to do: it holds by construction

AMENDMENTS 1.3, F-15's line. This row requires an object store (S jrnl +tier(store), footnote 1; SLOG's tier + obj) and keeps its restore mark in the store's manifest (A-08's conditional-create rows). Every new epoch is recorded there before it is used (E-33, a needed rule); a slot move raises the slot's epoch (P slot); so no move can open while the store is down, and F-15 lets only wake, new replicas and old history wait. With slot moves added to that list it is open: writes and failover use local journals only, and E-33's store was always reachable

ISR: old segments are uploaded behind the local log (S walg +tier, Kafka's KIP-405), so a down store should only hold retention back, and no partition moves (P fixN). Not run here; local logs grow while uploads wait

This row founds by fero init and requires no object store across boxes (S jrnl +tier), and A-08 leaves the home of its restore mark open, so the clash (a move waits for the store) is not shown for it; rows with no slot moves (CELL, SPLIT, LANE) have nothing on the write path that waits for the mark. rules.basis: Z crash is Raft as published, with no checksum per entry. TLC on etcd's spec: a voter that keeps its id and cuts one bad entry as a torn tail votes for a lagging candidate, and the new leader overwrites a committed write (one fault, 32 states, E-37). The fix is another row's option (rejoin or par)

With Z rejoin (A-28) a checksum per entry finds the bad entry, the replica wipes itself and returns as a new one that never votes under its old id: TLC on etcd's spec explored all 27,985 states, all 10 invariants hold, no committed write is lost (E-37). PD's judges name par as the other fix: it repairs the entry from a peer and keeps the vote (E-37, 7 rules, three voters, no membership change). Whether one bad entry wipes one group or the whole journal is K-24
